turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I want to stop buying coffee every morning and make it at home instead.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good plan, you'll save a lot. Do you want something simple like a French press, or are you ready to invest in an espresso machine?

think_reask: So, a simple French press, or going all in with an espresso machine?
Okay, what's it going to be for your home coffee, press or espresso machine?
welcome_back: Welcome back. You were choosing how to make coffee at home, a press or an espresso machine?
Hi again. Decided between the French press and the espresso machine?

endings.user: French press. I just want something that works at six in the morning.
endings.moshi: Great choice. Use coarse ground coffee and let it steep for about four minutes.

endings.user: Espresso. I mostly drink lattes, so I might as well.
endings.moshi: Then get one with a steam wand for the milk. It'll pay for itself in a few months.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm meeting a friend I haven't seen in years.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: How nice. Would you prefer a cozy little cafe where you can talk for hours, or somewhere livelier in the town centre?

contexts.pending: cozy quiet cafe or livelier place in town
think_reask: So, a quiet cozy cafe or somewhere busier in town?
Time's up. What kind of place feels right for catching up?
welcome_back: Welcome back. You were picking a cafe for meeting your old friend, quiet or lively?
There you are. Still thinking about where to meet your friend?

endings.user: Somewhere quiet. We've got years to catch up on.
endings.moshi: Then go mid-morning on a weekday, when cafes are calmest.

endings.user: Lively, actually. It might feel less awkward with some noise around.
endings.moshi: That's a good instinct. A busy cafe with a nice terrace would be perfect.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I think I'm drinking way too much coffee. Like five cups a day.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a fair amount. Would you rather cut down gradually, or switch some of those cups to decaf?

contexts.pending: cut down gradually or switch some cups to decaf
think_reask: So, cutting down slowly, or swapping a few cups for decaf?
Okay, which feels more doable, fewer cups or some decaf?
welcome_back: Welcome back. We were talking about your coffee habit. Cut down, or try decaf?
Hi again. Have you thought about how you want to drink less coffee?

endings.user: Decaf in the afternoon. I still want the ritual.
endings.moshi: That's a nice approach. You keep the habit and probably sleep better too.

endings.user: Cut down. One cup less each week until I'm at two.
endings.moshi: Very sensible. Drink some water when you'd normally reach for a cup, it helps.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: {friend}, did you finish the milk?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: There should be a little left, check behind the juice.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Found it. Barely enough for one coffee.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Make it for yourself. I'll grab one on the way to work.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Are you sure? I can share it.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: No, really. There's a new place near the station I want to try anyway.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Which beans did you buy this time?

turns.text: Some Ethiopian ones. The guy at the market said they're fruity.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Fruity coffee? That sounds wrong.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Just try it. It tastes a bit like berries, honestly.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Fine. Should I grind them fine or coarse for the pour-over?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Medium, like sand. Not too fine or it gets bitter.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Medium, okay. I'll make us both one.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: {friend}, what's that thing you ordered last time? The cold one?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Cold brew with oat milk. It's really smooth.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is it strong? I don't want to be awake all night.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Pretty strong. Maybe get a small one.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or I'll just have a tea and steal a sip of yours.

turns.speaker: friend

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What's the difference between a latte and a flat white?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A flat white has less milk and a thinner layer of foam, so it tastes stronger. A latte is bigger and milkier.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And a cappuccino?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A cappuccino has a thick layer of foam on top, and it's usually smaller than a latte.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So if I want something / not too milky but still creamy?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A flat white is probably your best bet. Strong coffee flavour with a smooth, velvety texture.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, I'm going to order one tomorrow and see.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Enjoy it. If it's too strong, you can always ask for an extra splash of milk.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My coffee from the drip machine always tastes bitter. What am I doing wrong?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A few things can cause that. Are you using pre-ground coffee, and how long does it sit on the hot plate?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Pre-ground, and it sits there most of the morning.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's likely it. The hot plate keeps cooking the coffee, which makes it bitter. Try pouring it into a thermos right after brewing.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, I'd never have guessed that. Anything else?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Clean the machine with vinegar every month or so. Old oils and scale build up and taste awful.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don't think I've ever / descaled it, to be honest.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then you'll probably notice a big difference. Run a couple of rounds of plain water afterwards to rinse it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How late in the day can I drink coffee and still sleep?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Caffeine stays in your system for quite a while, about half of it is still there five or six hours later. Many people stop around early afternoon.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So no coffee after lunch?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: If you go to bed around eleven, try to have your last cup by about two. Everyone's a bit different though.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about decaf? Is that / totally caffeine free?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not totally, but close. A cup of decaf has only a tiny amount, so it's usually fine in the evening.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Great, decaf after dinner it is.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sounds like a good compromise. You keep the taste without the sleepless night.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I want to make iced coffee at home this summer. Where do I start?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: The easiest way is to brew your coffee a bit stronger than usual and pour it over lots of ice, so it doesn't get watery.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about cold brew? Is that hard?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's really easy, just slow. Mix coarse coffee with cold water, leave it in the fridge overnight, and strain it in the morning.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How long does it keep?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: About a week in the fridge. Make a big jar on Sunday and you're set for the week.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Actually, maybe I'll / try both and see which I like.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good idea. Freeze some coffee in an ice cube tray too, so your drink never gets diluted.

option_sets.lead_in: I want to start making better coffee at home, and I've got a few choices.
options: The first one is a French press, cheap and simple, but you have to clean out the grounds.
Then there's a pour over cone, which makes a really clean cup but takes some practice.
Option three is a pod machine, super fast and easy, but the pods add up over time.
And the last one is an espresso machine with a milk steamer, which is pretty expensive.
moshi_comment: If you love lattes, the espresso machine is the only one that really gets you there, but it's a big investment. For plain black coffee, the French press or pour over give great flavor for little money. The pod machine wins on convenience but not taste.
Do you usually drink your coffee black or with milk? If it's black, I'd start with the pour over, it's cheap and rewarding. If you want milk drinks, the espresso machine is worth saving for.

option_sets.lead_in: I can't figure out which coffee beans to order for the office.
options: One is a dark roast that's bold and smoky, the kind most people expect from office coffee.
Another is a light roast from a small farm, fruity and bright, but some people find it sour.
Or we could get a medium blend that's smooth and balanced and a bit cheaper by the pound.
moshi_comment: For a whole office, the medium blend is the safest choice, it pleases most people and saves money. The dark roast is good if your coworkers like it strong with milk. The light roast is lovely but might get complaints.
Do people mostly drink it with milk and sugar? If so, the dark roast holds up better. If not, the medium blend is a nice middle ground.
